messages:
SRE Bot: [ALERT] sustained GPU pod failures in eu-west serving clusters. Autoscaler reports extreme churn (rapid scale-up/scale-down) and we have elevated 5xx rates on hosted text-generation routes. Pager triggered for oncall.

jane_oncall: I'm looking. Dashboards show cluster autoscaler adding a bunch of nodes then removing them within minutes. PodRestartCount and OOMKilled on model containers. Impact: ~12% error rate, latency tail at 99p blown up. Dedicated customer pools unaffected.

alex_runtime: grabbing recent logs from a failing pod: 
```:
2026-03-15T04:02:11Z model-server[pid=2245]: allocation error: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T04:02:12Z kubelet: pod inference-gpu-9c2 aborting with status 137
2026-03-15T04:02:12Z nvidia-smi[info]: GPU 0 mem: 15433 MiB / 16384 MiB, fragmentation: high
```
This looks like many pods concurrently trying to load full model weights after node provisioning; fragmentation and leaks make available contiguous memory insufficient.

miguel_sre: Autoscaler timeline: 08:01:30 scaleUp -> +20 nodes, 08:03:10 scaleDown -> -18 nodes, 08:06:00 scaleUp -> +15 nodes. No damping configured for rapid resizes. ASG spot interruptions also visible for some nodes causing eviction cycles.

jane_oncall: I want quick mitigations: slow autoscaler rate, cordon noisy nodes, route public traffic to a lighter model variant, restart driver daemons. Support prepare public message.

olivia_support: Draft status: "We are investigating intermittent errors and increased latency for hosted generation in eu-west. Engineers are working on mitigations; some requests may be served by a smaller model temporarily." Approve to post?

jane_oncall: Post now. I'll update every 15 minutes. Notify enterprise slack and CS for any VIP tickets.

alex_runtime: Suggestions queued: 
- set CA --balance-similar-node-groups and apply a scale-up-rate limit (--max-node-provision 3)
- add a 10m scale-down-delay
- temporarily taint new nodes to prevent immediate scheduling until warmup hook completes
- implement podTopologySpread and maxConcurrentModelLoads admission hook
- enable lazy weight loading in model-server canary

miguel_sre: I'm applying CA flags now. Also enabling annotation to stop scale-down for the affected nodegroup while we stabilize.

devops_bot: cluster-autoscaler updated (job id 9281). Flags: --max-node-provision=3 --scale-down-delay=600s.

jane_oncall: cordoning and draining the worst offenders to stop noisy reschedules: 
```:
kubectl cordon n-gpu-014
kubectl drain n-gpu-014 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Draining moves pods onto already warmed nodes rather than newly provisioned ones.

alex_runtime: patched model-router to steer 70% public traffic to gpt-small-2026 and keep 100% enterprise on gpt-medium-2026. Config snippet applied via configmap.

devops_bot: model-router config reloaded successfully.

miguel_sre: Next: restart nvidia-driver plugin daemonset across nodes to clear leaked GPU allocations: 
```:
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-driver -n kube-system
```
Rolling restart in flight. If a node still reports GPU processes locked to kernel after driver restart, we'll reprovision (terminate instance) so ASG replaces it cleanly.

jane_oncall: support message updated: "Mitigations applied to reduce failures; expected service improvement in 10-20 minutes. Some requests may route to a smaller model." Posted.

alex_runtime: observed immediate drop in number of new pending pods; autoscaler events slowed. However, a small set of pods still hit OOM during init due to heavy pre-allocation in model-server. Initiating a canary build with lazy weight load flag: --defer-heavy-alloc.

miguel_sre: after driver restarts and node reprovisions for 4 problematic machines, GPU memory pressure normalized. Current GPU OOM Kills: 3 over last 18 minutes (down from 42). CA churn back to baseline after 25 minutes. Recommend leaving CA damping for 1 hour before revert.

jane_oncall: handoff: @miguel_sre you'll own stabilization and rollback plan; I'll manage comms and timeline drafting. Summary for handoff: root cause chain: rapid autoscaler scale-ups + many pods trying to load large model binaries concurrently -> memory fragmentation/leaks on GPUs -> OOMKills & crashloops -> scale-downs too fast causing node flaps and further evictions. Mitigations applied: CA rate limits and scale-down delay, cordon/drain noisy nodes, driver daemonset restart, temporary model fallback for public traffic, canary for lazy loads.

olivia_support: Notifying affected customers flagged by eu-west headers. Using template: "We have applied mitigations; monitoring indicates reduction in errors. We will follow up with a postmortem."

miguel_sre: follow-ups I'm tracking: 
- collect CA event timeline and correlate with ASG interruption events
- gather per-pod GPU mem histograms and fragmentation metrics
- code change: admission-control to limit concurrent model initializations per node (soft quota)
- add warmup lifecycle hook to node bootstrap to set a 1-minute scheduling delay for heavy workloads

alex_runtime: I'll open PR for default podTopologySpread and for a model-server flag to limit concurrent loader threads. Also adding telemetry to expose model load memory high-water marks.

devops_bot: automatic check: success rate for GPU model pods improved from 76% -> 97% in last 20 minutes. No further OOM spikes detected.

jane_oncall: incident classified SEV-2. Oncall handoff scheduled in 30m. I'll draft timeline and blameless postmortem items. Keep CA damping in place until we confirm a full hour of stable behavior.

miguel_sre: handing off to operations rotation for watch. I'll attach CA patch diffs and node list to the incident doc.

SRE Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, error rate trending down, partial customer impact persists (~4% of requests). Next update in 15 minutes. Channel remains open.

jane_oncall: closing pager handoff. Thanks everyone. We'll do a retro and push the admission-control and lazy-load fixes as high priority action items.

olivia_support: acknowledged and keeping CS informed.
